=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/security_audit_causality.py: lines 420-433 (LAST RUN DIFF additions inside `_revalidate_waiver`)
  Problem: The new block performs a second `_snapshot(repo, current_head)` plus `_target_symbol` and `_scope_for_target`, even though the earlier `analyze(repo, file_name, line, audited_head, current_head)` call at the same `current_head` already computed the target symbol and its reverse-caller scope. The duplicate BFS over every Python symbol in the repository runs the iterative `_scope_for_target` walk twice on the same head SHA.
  Why it fails at runtime: each revalidate-waiver invocation now pays for two `git archive --format=tar $current_head` calls and two iterative reverse-caller walks for the same SHA. For a repo where `_scope_for_target` walks dozens of modules, this doubles the wall-clock latency of the security-pass waiver gate, which already runs once per finding per cycle.
  Severity: NIT
  Issue confidence: 3
- scripts/security_audit_causality.py: lines 422-429 (LAST RUN DIFF)
  Problem: When `analyze` succeeded and returned `causal_scope_status == "complete"`, but the new second pass's `_target_symbol` returns `None`, the function returns `{"valid": False, "reason": "repository causal graph is unavailable"}`. That message conflates two states: (a) the graph was genuinely unreadable, and (b) the graph was readable to `analyze` but `_target_symbol` did not select a symbol at this line.
  Why it fails at runtime: if the `_target_symbol` ordering change introduced in the original PR (`__module__` last) ever selects a different symbol than `analyze`'s internal selection for the same `(symbols, file_name, line)`, the function silently downgrades to a misleading "graph unavailable" reason instead of the more accurate "current causal target is unavailable". Operators chasing the diagnostic would re-run with `--repo` instead of investigating why the target selection differs.
  Severity: NIT
  Issue confidence: 3
- scripts/security_audit_causality.py: line 422 (`_snapshot(repo, current_head)` repeated after `analyze` already snapshotted)
  Problem: Same `current_head` SHA is snapshotted twice per revalidate-waiver call. Each `_snapshot` runs `git archive --format=tar $ref -- *` and parses the tarball; for a repo with hundreds of Python files the second invocation duplicates the I/O and parse cost of the first.
  Why it fails at runtime: revalidate-waiver runs once per waiver per cycle, bounded by `MAX_SECURITY_PASS_CYCLES=5`. Two tar archives per call adds a fixed per-call multiplier to the security-pass critical path without changing correctness, because both calls receive the same `current_head` SHA and produce the same symbol list.
  Severity: NIT
  Issue confidence: 4
- scripts/security_audit_causality.py: line 449 (`if any(symbol.references.intersection(causal_reference_names) for symbol in changed_symbols):`)
  issue: A changed Python module can evade the new check by importing a scope function through an alias (`from app import sink as p_sink; def route(user): return p_sink(user)`). `p_sink` is a `Name.Load` (so it lands in `public_route.references`) but `sink` is not, and `p_sink` is not in `causal_reference_names`, so the intersection is empty.
  suggested minimal fix: in the changed-module scan, also accept any changed module whose `visit_ImportFrom` aliases point at a name present in `causal_reference_names` (extend `_CallCollector` to record the original `name` alongside each `asname`, then expand the intersection with the alias-resolved original names). Roughly 6-8 lines.
  estimated lines changed: 8
  Hardening risk score: 3
- scripts/security_audit_causality.py: line 428 (`if current_scope_ambiguous:`)
  issue: `_scope_for_target` reports `ambiguous=True` whenever the reverse-caller BFS visited the same symbol twice; this is a conservative signal but the current code returns the same `{"valid": False, "reason": "repository causal graph is ambiguous"}` reason text regardless of whether the ambiguity is at the file, function, or wildcard-import level. Operators cannot tell whether to widen `SECURITY_PASS_OWNERSHIP_CONTEXT_LINES` or remove a wildcard import.
  suggested minimal fix: include the specific `symbol.qualified_name` of the ambiguity source in the reason payload (e.g., `reason=f"repository causal graph is ambiguous at {name}"`). Roughly 2 lines.
  estimated lines changed: 2
  Hardening risk score: 1

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/security_audit_causality.py: Line 18 (SCHEMA constant) and lines 34, 77, 95-108 (references field and _CallCollector)
  Problem: The Symbol.calls field was renamed to Symbol.references and the _CallCollector semantics expanded from function-call targets only to all Name.Load nodes (variable reads, attribute lookups, etc.). This changes which symbols are selected as reverse callers, which changes causal_scope_files, which changes the fingerprint. Existing waivers computed with the old semantics will have different fingerprints under the new semantics, causing all pre-existing waivers to be rejected as "current causal scope changed" at line 403.
  Why it fails at runtime: A waiver created before this change has a fingerprint computed with the narrower `calls` semantics. After this change, the same finding produces a broader `references`-based fingerprint. The revalidation at lines 399-403 compares the new fingerprint against the stored fingerprint and rejects the waiver. The schema constant at line 18 remains "security_audit_causal_scope.v1" despite the semantic change, so the breaking change is not explicit in the schema version.
  Severity: NIT
  Issue confidence: 4
  Note: This breaking change may be intentional (the PR hardens security by broadening the causal scope). If so, consider bumping SCHEMA to "security_audit_causal_scope.v2" to make the incompatibility explicit. Existing waivers will be invalidated regardless, but a schema version bump documents the contract change.
